core_condition: at least one measured effect recorded in observed_effects from Ventora telemetry or public corpora

evidence.rationale: The general phenomena are empirically supported: Lindgaard et al. (2006) demonstrated that visual judgements of web pages form within ~50ms and correlate strongly with judgements at longer exposure; Tractinsky and colleagues showed the consistency of immediate aesthetic perception; the advertising-avoidance literature (Cho & Cheon 2004 and the banner-blindness work following it) establishes systematic avoidance of ad-like elements. Scored 2 rather than 3 because the field mixes solid experimental work with a large body of practitioner claims of uncertain provenance, and because the specific patterns most often cited (F-shaped scanning, fold behaviour) are task- and layout-dependent rather than general laws — see dissent.

product_applicability.rationale: Directly implementable and cross-cutting: single dominant element per view, front-loaded meaning in headings and labels, avoidance of advertising idiom for genuine content. Applies to every surface a visitor samples rather than reads.

measurability.rationale: Downstream proxies are reachable (bounce, conversion, engagement with the primary action), but attention itself is not observable in our telemetry — the literature's instrument is eye-tracking, which we do not have. We infer from behaviour, and the same design changes also move load and fluency, so attribution is weak. Scored 2 honestly.

orthogonality.rationale: Overlaps CL-14 (scanning as an adaptation to capacity limits) and MM-15 (signalling is the design response to selective attention). Retained as distinct because it describes an empirically observed allocation behaviour — including ad avoidance, which none of the others predict — rather than a capacity constraint or a combination rule.

safety.rationale: The mechanism describes where attention goes, which makes it directly usable to steer attention away from things. Three hard rules address this: no disguised advertising exploiting native-content avoidance (explicitly regulated), no placing or styling material information where scanning predictably misses it, and no aggressive attention-hijacking techniques (motion, fake system cues). Score 2 rather than 3 because the misuse — hiding what should be seen — is subtle, common, and harder to detect than a fake countdown.

dissent: This is the mechanism in S7 most contaminated by practitioner folklore, and the dossier records that plainly. (1) Much of what is repeated as established — the F-shaped reading pattern, fixed assumptions about the fold, universal scan paths — originates in small-sample industry studies rather than peer-reviewed experiments, and the peer-reviewed eye-tracking literature shows scan patterns varying substantially with task (searching versus browsing), layout, expertise and device. We therefore claim selective, non-linear sampling and fast first impressions, and explicitly do not encode any specific scan geometry. (2) The evidence base skews to desktop web pages from an earlier era; mobile interfaces and feed-based consumption, which dominate now, are underrepresented, so generalisation to those contexts is an assumption. (3) Banner blindness is not absolute: recent work finds that relevance, creativity and personalisation can materially reduce avoidance, which means the avoidance is of *perceived irrelevance in advertising form* rather than of a visual shape per se. (4) The 50-millisecond finding concerns aesthetic/affective judgement, not comprehension or decision quality — it is frequently over-read as 'you have 50ms to convince', which the study does not support. The corpus for this mechanism also required a re-harvest after the original terms collided with scanning microscopy and web-server literature; the current corpus is on-topic but the review anchor filter still found no qualifying topical review, so coverage rests on pins and term breadth.

evidence_sources.ref: Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek & Brown (2006). Attention web designers: You have 50 milliseconds to make a good first impression. Behaviour & Information Technology 25(2).
Cho & Cheon (2004). Why do people avoid advertising on the internet? Journal of Advertising 33(4).
Tractinsky et al. — consistency of immediate aesthetic perceptions of web pages (2006).
Contemporary banner-blindness work on relevance/creativity moderators (Yang et al. 2021; Abedi et al. 2022).

notes: Cross-checked against /corpora/evidence/SC-17.json (390 records after re-harvest with corrected terms; the original harvest was discarded as polluted by 'scanning'/'web' collisions — proteomics, microscopy, scintigraphy). Review anchor still not found (D-034 honest report). Cross-cutting mechanism: parent S7. Total 11 at threshold, driven by evidence 2, measurability 2 and safety 2 — the weakest-evidence mechanism in the perception node, admitted because the core phenomena are real and the design consequences are unavoidable, but claimed narrowly and without any specific scan-pattern dogma. Verdict INCUBATING; CORE strictly on a measured effect.
